newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S TELKOM DENIES STIFLING INTERNET RIVALS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S TELKOM DENIES STIFLING INTERNET RIVALS.

text.p: South African utility Telkom denied on Tuesday that it was stifling competition in the Internet connection industry through its South African Internet Exchange (SAIX).
Telkom wants the service to be subject to exclusivity under the 1996 Telecommunications Act, prompting charges by some industry firms that it will kill off rival networks.
But Telkom argues SAIX is a backbone highway that provides access and transport only, allowing Internet service providers to offer added-value services.

"We are encouraging the establishment of new service providers on the SAIX network by lowering the barriers to entry. Exactly one year after the launch of SAIX we now have 42 service providers on our network," said Pinky Mohali, Telkom group executive for regulatory affairs.
Several Internet Service Providers (ISPs) have argued that Telkom is using unfair business practises by cross-subsidising its Internet services with cash from its other interests.
"Telkom is trying to justify making Internet provision a basic service and that is ludicrous," Philip Esselaar, joint chairman of the Internet Service Providers' Association, said recently.
Telkom and representatives from the Internet industry are currently in talks with the South African Telecommunicatins Regulatory Authority (Satra) in a bid to settle their dispute.
Satra has recently advertised for auditors to check Telkom accounts for cross-subsidisation and discriminatory pricing.
"We recognise that all ISPs are our customers and we are confident that Satra will find a solution which is satisfactory to all parties," Moholi said.
